text:
Anna Chen: seeing a sustained p99 CPU spike on telemetry-ingest since last deploy, looks correlated with exporter batching/window change. examples: p99 ingest CPU 82% -> 96% on collector nodes

telemetry-bot: ALERT: collector-ingest-#3 CPU > 90% for 6m (group: telemetry-ingest)

Raj Patel: can you paste the OTEL config and the timeline of the deploy?

Anna Chen: deploy started 2034566000, reverted 2034569000 briefly, then rolled forward. config change was: increased batching window from 200ms -> 800ms and enabled kv-cache prefetch for span keys

Anna Chen: snippet:
```
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_BATCH_TIMEOUT=800ms
TELEM_KV_PREFETCH_ENABLED=true
TELEM_KV_PREFETCH_DEPTH=64
```

Miles O'Connor: interesting — larger batch window should reduce exporter overhead but can increase KV cache churn if prefetch expands active set. are we seeing more unique span keys?

Anna Chen: yes, index of unique span.name tags went up ~2.6x during the window (sampled), and memory for kv cache around same time jumped 30%

Leah Gomez: quick idea: bigger batch window increases time a span sits in memory waiting to flush; with prefetch we might be loading adjacent prefixes and evicting hot slices. that causes more backend lookups -> CPU. can we flip prefetch off and keep batch window?

Samir Kaur: +1 to testing prefetch off. also try shrinking batch size or using adaptive batching with max_latency 250ms as a canary. We should A/B the change behind a rollout flag.

Raj Patel: how about exporter concurrency? if batching latency increases, exporter goroutines might pile up. what is OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_MAX_CONCURRENCY?

Anna Chen: default is 16 in our image. we didn't change it. logs show exporter goroutine count rising during the spike. paste of debug logs:
```
[2034567001] exporter: send loop blocked, queue=12456, goroutines=58
[2034567023] kvcache: evict key=service:api:foo size=34kb reason=overcommit
```

Miles O'Connor: that log matches eviction thrash. hypothesis: prefetch depth 64 + bigger batch window = temporally higher working set -> cache churn -> CPU + GC pressure.

Leah Gomez: action plan proposal:
1) revert TELEM_KV_PREFETCH_ENABLED -> false on canary nodes
2) limit batch_timeout to 250ms for canary
3) observe p99 CPU and exporter queue length for 30m
4) if improves, roll to remaining nodes with monitoring alert thresholds

Samir Kaur: also add a quick experiment: same batch window but reduce prefetch depth to 8 and enable sampling of low-card spans. we might get similar cost with better tail behavior.

Anna Chen: starting canary change on node group telemetry-canary-2 now. will post metrics in 15m.

telemetry-bot: DEPLOY: rollout telemetry-canary-2 config change by anna_ch (ID: dpl-88233) at 2034569800

Raj Patel: can someone create a lightweight k6 load test to reproduce span volume pattern? we need deterministic repro for benchmarking changes.

Miles O'Connor: I have a script that can replay sampled traces with high cardinality names. I'll run it against canary later today.

Anna Chen: early numbers after 12m: p99 CPU on canary down from 95% -> 66%, exporter queue length steady ~40 vs 120 previously, GC pause p99 down 40%

Leah Gomez: great signal. if sustained at 30m we can promote change and then try prefetch depth reduction experiment.

Samir Kaur: please add a dashboard tile with exporter_queue_len, kvcache_evictions/s, p99_cpu, and batch_latency on the rollout page so PMs can see it. also link the rollout to the eval suite.

Anna Chen: will update rollout notes and add the dashboard links. thanks all :thumbsup:
